claim: Up to 50 cavins associate on a caveola
source: We show that up to 50 cavins associate on a caveola.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by single-molecule fluorescence analysis showing cavin1 forms complexes containing 50 ± 5 proteins (Figure 1H and related text).

claim: Cavin1, cavin2, and cavin3 do not form a single coat complex containing all three family members
source: However, rather than forming a single coat complex containing the three cavin family members, single-molecule analysis reveals an exquisite specificity of interactions between cavin1, cavin2 and cavin3.
evidence: Single-molecule coincidence analysis shows segregation of cavin2 and cavin3 (Figure 2C, 2F, 3A), supported by ALPHAScreen assays showing no interaction between cavin2 and cavin3 (Figure 2H, 2I).

claim: Changes in membrane tension can flatten caveolae and cause release of the cavin coat
source: Changes in membrane tension can flatten the caveolae, causing the release of the cavin coat and its disassembly into separate cavin1-cavin2 and cavin1-cavin3 subcomplexes.
evidence: Hypo-osmotic treatment experiments show dissociation of cavin coat into subcomplexes (Figure 4A-G), with single-molecule analysis demonstrating segregation of cavin2 and cavin3 after membrane stretch.

claim: Cavin subcomplexes contain 9 ± 2 cavin molecules
source: Each of these subcomplexes contain 9 ± 2 cavin molecules and appear to be the building blocks of the caveolar coat.
evidence: Single-molecule brightness analysis after hypo-osmotic treatment shows oligomers composed of 9 ± 2 cavin1 proteins (Figure 4C and related text).

claim: Cavin1-cavin2 and cavin1-cavin3 subcomplexes form individual striations on the surface of caveolae
source: High resolution immunoelectron microscopy suggests a remarkable nanoscale organization of these separate subcomplexes, forming individual striations on the surface of caveolae.
evidence: Immuno-EM shows spatial separation between cavin2 and cavin3 within individual caveolae (Figure 5C), with bivariate clustering analysis confirming significantly lower co-clustering of cavin2-cavin3 compared to cavin1-cavin3 (Figure 5D).

claim: Approximately 140 CAV1 molecules associate with a single caveola in mammalian cells
source: Approximately 140 CAV1 molecules associate with a single caveola in mammalian cells (Pelkmans and Zerial, 2005) and in a model prokaryotic system upon caveolin expression (Walser et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Caveolae possess a unique cytoplasmically facing striated coat enriched in CAV1
source: Caveolae possess a unique cytoplasmically facing striated coat enriched in CAV1 (Rothberg et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to previous work.

claim: Cavin1 forms homo-complexes in MCF-7 cells
source: As shown in Figure 2A,B, in the cytosol of MCF-7 cells cavin1 forms homo-complexes but also stable heteromeric complexes when expressed with cavin2 or cavin3.
evidence: Single-molecule coincidence analysis shows cavin1-GFP and cavin1-Cherry co-diffuse (Figure 1C, 2A).

claim: Cavin1 forms stable heteromeric complexes with cavin2
source: As shown in Figure 2A,B, in the cytosol of MCF-7 cells cavin1 forms homo-complexes but also stable heteromeric complexes when expressed with cavin2 or cavin3.
evidence: Single-molecule coincidence analysis shows mixed oligomers of cavin1-GFP and cavin2-Cherry (Figure 2A, 2D).

claim: Cavin1 forms stable heteromeric complexes with cavin3
source: As shown in Figure 2A,B, in the cytosol of MCF-7 cells cavin1 forms homo-complexes but also stable heteromeric complexes when expressed with cavin2 or cavin3.
evidence: Single-molecule coincidence analysis shows mixed oligomers of cavin1-GFP and cavin3-Cherry (Figure 2B, 2E).

claim: Cavin2 and cavin3 do not form mixed oligomers when co-expressed
source: Strikingly, we could not detect any mixed oligomers when cavin2 and cavin3 were co-expressed. Figure 2C demonstrates that co-expressions lead to two segregated populations of cavin2-cavin2 and cavin3-cavin3 oligomers.
evidence: Single-molecule coincidence analysis shows no mixed oligomers between cavin2-GFP and cavin3-Cherry (Figure 2C, 2F), confirmed by ALPHAScreen assays (Figure 2H, 2I) and pull-down experiments (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).

claim: Cavin1 oligomer assembly occurs within 15 minutes at nanomolar concentrations
source: Surprisingly, we found that most of the cavin1 protein assembled into oligomers within the first 15 min while the concentration was still below 10 nM (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Real-time observation of cavin1-GFP production in cell-free system shows formation of large amplitude bursts within 15 minutes at concentrations below 10 nM (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).

claim: A maximum of approximately 30% of cavin3 can be incorporated into cavin1 oligomers
source: On the contrary, we found that only a maximum of ca. 30% of cavin3 could be incorporated into cavin1 oligomers (Figure 2E).
evidence: Cell-free co-expression experiments with varying ratios show limited incorporation of cavin3 into cavin1 oligomers (Figure 2E).

claim: Cavin1 does not act as a bridge between cavin2 and cavin3
source: Figure 2I shows that the presence of cavin1 did not enhance the interaction of cavin2 and 3.
evidence: ALPHAScreen assays with co-expression of cavin1, cavin2, and cavin3 show no interaction between cavin2 and cavin3 even in the presence of cavin1 (Figure 2I). Single-molecule analysis in MCF-7 cells co-expressing cavin1-FLAG with cavin2-Cherry and cavin3-GFP confirms lack of interaction (Figure 3A).

claim: Each caveola contains three to four times more CAV1 than cavin1
source: The coincidence peak is centred between C = 0.25 and C = 0.3, indicating that each caveola contains three to four times more CAV1 than cavin1.
evidence: Single-molecule coincidence analysis between cavin1-Cherry and CAV1-GFP shows coincidence peak centered at C = 0.25-0.3 (Figure 3B), and brightness analysis shows CAV1 signal is 3.5 times brighter than cavin1 (Figure 3C).

claim: The number of cavin1 per caveola is estimated between 40 and 50
source: Both methods suggest that the number of cavin1 per caveolae is estimated, again, between 40 and 50.
evidence: Brightness analysis and coincidence measurements of cavin1 with CAV1 in MCF-7 cells indicate 40-50 cavin1 molecules per caveola.

claim: The presence of CAV1 narrows the distribution of cavin1 particle sizes to around 60 nm
source: However, while the apparent number of subunits per cavin1 assembly has not significantly changed, the presence of CAV1 had a pronounced effect on the distribution of particle sizes (Figure 1J; Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), narrowing the distribution to around 60 nm, which corresponds to the typical size of a caveola.
evidence: Comparison of size distributions shows CAV1 narrows cavin1 complex size distribution to ~60 nm (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: Cavin2 and cavin3 co-localize on the same caveolae when CAV1 and cavin1 are present
source: We observed coincidental diffusion of cavin2 and cavin3 indicating that they were part of the same assembly (Figure 3D).
evidence: Single-molecule analysis in MCF-7 cells co-expressing CAV1, cavin1-FLAG, cavin2-Cherry, and cavin3-GFP shows coincidental diffusion (Figure 3D). Similar results obtained in HeLa cells with endogenous CAV1 and cavin1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).

claim: Hypo-osmotic treatment reduces the apparent size of cavin1 complexes to less than 30 nm
source: The dual-colour experiment showed that the cavin1 oligomer recovered in the cytosolic fraction diffuses much faster than the caveolae bound protein: the apparent size of the cavin1 complex is reduced to ‹ 30 nm (calculated as diameter of a diffusing spherical object) (Figure 4A).
evidence: Single-molecule analysis after hypo-osmotic treatment shows reduction in apparent size from 60 nm to ~20 nm (Figure 4A).

claim: After hypo-osmotic treatment, cavin1 remains oligomeric
source: Yet the protein remained oligomeric, as all fluorescent events register both fluorophores (Figure 4B).
evidence: Single-molecule coincidence analysis shows all bursts contain both GFP and Cherry fluorophores after hypo-osmotic treatment (Figure 4B).

claim: Hypo-osmotic treatment causes cavin2 and cavin3 to separate into two different subcomplexes
source: The absence of coincidence suggests that while cavin2 and cavin3 can localize to the same caveolae, their release from the membrane during stretch causes them to separate into two different subcomplexes.
evidence: Single-molecule coincidence analysis after hypo-osmotic treatment shows complete segregation of cavin2 and cavin3 (Figure 4F), with all cavin2 bound to cavin1 (Figure 4D) and all cavin3 bound to cavin1 (Figure 4E).

claim: The cavin1-cavin2 subcomplex has an apparent size of 30 nm
source: Interestingly, even the size of the two subcomplexes differs, with cavin1-cavin1 and cavin1-cavin3 forming oligomers of similar size (20 nm) that are significantly smaller than the cavin1-cavin2 sub-complex (30 nm).
evidence: Single-molecule size measurements after hypo-osmotic treatment show cavin1-cavin2 subcomplexes have average size of 30 nm (Figure 4G).

claim: The cavin1-cavin3 subcomplex has an apparent size of 20 nm
source: Interestingly, even the size of the two subcomplexes differs, with cavin1-cavin1 and cavin1-cavin3 forming oligomers of similar size (20 nm) that are significantly smaller than the cavin1-cavin2 sub-complex (30 nm).
evidence: Single-molecule size measurements after hypo-osmotic treatment show cavin1-cavin3 subcomplexes have average size of 20 nm (Figure 4G).

claim: Cavin1, cavin2, and cavin3 demonstrate immunolabeling consistent with a striated pattern
source: Cavin1 (Figure 5A–top two rows), cavin2 (Figure 5A–middle two rows) and cavin3 (Figure 5A–bottom two rows) respectively demonstrated immunolabeling consistent with a striated pattern.
evidence: Immuno-EM of unroofed 3T3-L1 fibroblasts shows striated labeling patterns for all three cavins (Figure 5A).

claim: Cavin1-Cherry and cavin3-GFP demonstrate close spatial association and co-label the same caveolae
source: In accordance with the single-molecule fluorescence data, cavin1-Cherry (3 nm gold–coloured red) and cavin3-GFP (7 nm gold–coloured green) demonstrated a close spatial association and co-labeled the same caveolae with no perceivable separation (Figure 5B).
evidence: Dual-labeling immuno-EM shows cavin1 and cavin3 co-localize on same caveolae without spatial separation (Figure 5B).

claim: Cavin2 and cavin3 localize to the same caveola but show significant spatial separation within individual caveolae
source: Dual-labeling of cavin2-GFP (7 nm–coloured green) and cavin3-Cherry (3 nm–coloured red), in cells expressing roughly equivalent amounts (with co-expression of cavin1-FLAG), demonstrated that cavin2 and cavin3 were localized to the same caveola (Figure 5C). However, within an individual caveola significant spatial separation between these proteins was observed, consistent with separate striations.
evidence: Dual-labeling immuno-EM shows cavin2 and cavin3 on same caveola but spatially separated (Figure 5C), confirmed by Ripley's K function bivariate analysis showing significantly lower co-clustering of cavin2-cavin3 compared to cavin1-cavin3 (Figure 5D).

claim: There is significantly lower co-clustering of cavin2-cavin3 compared to cavin1-cavin3
source: There was a significantly lower level of co-clustering of cavin2-cavin3 as compared to cavin1-cavin3 (Figure 5D).
evidence: Ripley's K function bivariate clustering analysis quantifies spatial relationships (Figure 5D).

claim: Caveolae are an abundant feature of the plasma membrane of many vertebrate cells
source: Caveolae are an abundant feature of the plasma membrane of many vertebrate cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Three caveolins are present in mammalian cells
source: Three caveolins are present in mammalian cells with caveolin-1 (CAV1) and caveolin-3 (CAV3) essential for caveolar formation in nonmuscle and muscle cells respectively.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: CAV1 is essential for caveolar formation in nonmuscle cells
source: Three caveolins are present in mammalian cells with caveolin-1 (CAV1) and caveolin-3 (CAV3) essential for caveolar formation in nonmuscle and muscle cells respectively.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: CAV3 is essential for caveolar formation in muscle cells
source: Three caveolins are present in mammalian cells with caveolin-1 (CAV1) and caveolin-3 (CAV3) essential for caveolar formation in nonmuscle and muscle cells respectively.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Caveolins bind cholesterol and fatty acids
source: Caveolins bind cholesterol and fatty acids and form homo-oligomers required for caveolar formation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Caveolins form homo-oligomers required for caveolar formation
source: Caveolins bind cholesterol and fatty acids and form homo-oligomers required for caveolar formation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Human patients lacking CAV1 show severe lipodystrophy
source: Human patients lacking CAV1 show a severe lipodystrophy while CAV3 mutations, many of which disrupt caveola formation in muscle, are associated with a number of muscle diseases.
evidence: This is stated as established clinical knowledge.

claim: CAV3 mutations are associated with muscle diseases
source: Human patients lacking CAV1 show a severe lipodystrophy while CAV3 mutations, many of which disrupt caveola formation in muscle, are associated with a number of muscle diseases.
evidence: This is stated as established clinical knowledge.

claim: Cavin1 was originally identified as a nuclear protein that can dissociate paused ternary transcription complexes
source: Cavin1 was originally identified as a nuclear protein that can dissociate paused ternary transcription complexes (Jansa et al., 1998), while cavin2 (Gustincich and Schneider, 1993) and cavin3 (Izumi et al., 1997) were identified as protein kinase C (PKC) substrates and have been suggested to function in the targeting of PKC to caveolae.
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: Cavin2 and cavin3 were identified as protein kinase C substrates
source: Cavin1 was originally identified as a nuclear protein that can dissociate paused ternary transcription complexes (Jansa et al., 1998), while cavin2 (Gustincich and Schneider, 1993) and cavin3 (Izumi et al., 1997) were identified as protein kinase C (PKC) substrates and have been suggested to function in the targeting of PKC to caveolae.
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Cavin4 is predominantly expressed in cardiac and skeletal muscle
source: Cavin4 is predominantly expressed in cardiac and skeletal muscle (Ogata et al., 2008; Tagawa et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Ablation of cavin1 expression causes loss of caveolae with CAV1 being released into the bulk membrane
source: Ablation of cavin1 expression causes loss of caveolae with CAV1 being released into the bulk membrane whereas expression of cavin1 or cavin2 in cells lacking cavins but expressing endogenous CAV1 is sufficient to generate caveolae (Hill et al., 2008; Hansen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Expression of cavin1 or cavin2 in cells lacking cavins but expressing endogenous CAV1 is sufficient to generate caveolae
source: Ablation of cavin1 expression causes loss of caveolae with CAV1 being released into the bulk membrane whereas expression of cavin1 or cavin2 in cells lacking cavins but expressing endogenous CAV1 is sufficient to generate caveolae (Hill et al., 2008; Hansen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Increased membrane tension causes caveolar flattening and dissociation of cavin1
source: This may be crucial for caveolar function in setting membrane tension and in mechanosensing as increased membrane tension causes caveolar flattening and dissociation of cavin1 (Sinha et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: The cavin proteins have conserved putative N-terminal coiled coil domains
source: Cavin1/polymerase transcript release factor (PTRF), cavin2/SDPR (serum deprivation response protein), cavin3/SRBC (serum deprivation response factor-related gene product that binds to C-kinase) and cavin4/MURC (muscle-restricted coiled-coil protein) are cytoplasmic proteins characterized by conserved putative N-terminal coiled coil domains (Hansen and Nichols, 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: The cavin proteins co-associate and form a cytosolic complex in cells lacking CAV1
source: The cavin proteins have been shown to co-associate and form a cytosolic complex(es) in cells lacking CAV1 (or CAV3), but are recruited to the cell surface to stabilize caveolae in cells expressing CAV1.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Cavin proteins are recruited to the cell surface to stabilize caveolae in cells expressing CAV1
source: The cavin proteins have been shown to co-associate and form a cytosolic complex(es) in cells lacking CAV1 (or CAV3), but are recruited to the cell surface to stabilize caveolae in cells expressing CAV1.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Caveolae form at the plasma membrane as caveolins and cavins associate, rather than earlier in the exocytic pathway
source: Furthermore, this cavin coat may provide a possible mechanism for spatial and temporal regulation of caveola formation: caveolae form at the plasma membrane as caveolins and cavins associate, rather than earlier in the exocytic pathway (Hill et al., 2008; Hayer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: The brightness of genetically encoded fluorophores such as eGFP and mCherry is considered too low to allow their individual detection when proteins are freely diffusing
source: The brightness of genetically encoded fluorophores such as the widely used eGFP and mCherry is considered too low to allow their individual detection, especially when proteins are freely diffusing and not immobilized on a surface.
evidence: This is stated as a technical limitation in the field.

claim: Cavin proteins show a tendency to degrade upon expression in E. coli
source: This is typically not possible with cavin proteins, which show a tendency to degrade upon expression in a bacterial host (Hansen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: MCF-7 cells are cavin and caveola-deficient
source: As MCF-7 cells are cavin and caveola-deficient the expressed cavin1 should be mostly in the cytosol.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the cell line used in experiments.

claim: GFP has a near-spherical β-barrel structure with a typical diameter of 5 nm
source: The structure of GFP is well known and the near-spherical β-barrel has a typical diameter of 5 nm.
evidence: This is stated as established structural knowledge.

claim: Cavin1 spontaneously assembles into a higher order structure of defined size even in the absence of CAV1
source: These data demonstrate that cavin1 spontaneously assembles into a higher order structure of defined size even in the absence of the scaffolding membrane protein CAV1.
evidence: Single-molecule analysis shows cavin1 forms large oligomers (~50 proteins) in MCF-7 cells lacking CAV1 (Figure 1H-J).

claim: The cavin1 oligomer has an apparent diameter of approximately 60 nm
source: If we assume that the cavin1 oligomer forms an isotropic complex and if we simplify its shape to a sphere, we can estimate the diameter of the diffusing object to approximately 60 nm (Figure 1J).
evidence: Residence time measurements and calibration against GFP indicate cavin1 oligomers have apparent diameter of ~60 nm (Figure 1J).

claim: The composition of oligomers formed by co-expression of cavin1 and cavin2 varies with levels of expression
source: We observed that the composition of oligomers formed by co-expression of cavin1 and 2 varied with levels of expression resulting in continuous transition from cavin-1 to cavin-2 homo-oligomer (Figure 2D).
evidence: Cell-free expression with varying DNA ratios shows full range of stoichiometries for cavin1-cavin2 oligomers (Figure 2D).

claim: Cavin oligomer assembly is a very rapid process that operates spontaneously at nanomolar concentrations
source: This indicates that cavin oligomer assembly is a very rapid process that operates spontaneously at nanomolar concentrations.
evidence: Real-time observation shows cavin1 assembles into oligomers within 15 minutes at concentrations below 10 nM (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).

claim: A typical caveola contains approximately 5 cavin subcomplexes
source: We find that when caveolae are disassembled by membrane stretch, cavins are released as subcomplexes of ∼9 cavin molecules, suggesting a typical caveola contains typically 5 cavin subcomplexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that caveolae contain ~50 cavins total and subcomplexes contain ~9 cavins each (50/9 ≈ 5).

claim: Each cavin subcomplex may be composed of three trimers
source: Cavin1 is believed to form trimers, possibly through a coiled-coil domain (Ludwig et al., 2013), suggesting that each sub-complex may be composed of three trimers.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that subcomplexes contain ~9 cavins and cavin1 forms trimers (3 trimers × 3 = 9).

claim: The cavin coat is made of multiple stable subcomplexes that can be released from caveolae without being disassembled into monomers
source: This suggests that the cavin coat is actually made of multiple stable subcomplexes that can be released from the caveolae without being disassembled into monomers.
evidence: Hypo-osmotic treatment releases cavin oligomers of ~9 proteins rather than monomers (Figure 4B, 4C).

claim: Cavin subcomplexes can reversibly assemble on a caveola
source: Because the cavins have such a high propensity to oligomerise, it is possible that the subcomplexes would form in the cytosol before reaching the CAV1-rich membrane, and that the subcomplexes can reversibly assemble on a caveola.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cavins oligomerize rapidly at low concentrations and can dissociate from caveolae as intact subcomplexes upon membrane stretch.

claim: The ratio of CAV1 to cavin determined biochemically is 4:1
source: A ratio of CAV1 to cavin of 4:1 determined biochemically (Ludwig et al., 2013) is in good agreement with the brightness analysis and CAV1-cavin1 coincidence data presented here.
evidence: This is stated with citation to another study and noted to agree with the current findings.

claim: The ratio of cavin1 to cavin3 is approximately 2:1
source: Similarly, the ratio of cavin1 to cavin3 of ∼2:1 is in excellent agreement with the result obtained from quantitative pull-downs (Ludwig et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to another study and noted to agree with the current findings.

claim: The ratio of cavin1 to cavin2 in subcomplexes released from caveolae is 2:1
source: The same ratio of 2:1 of cavin1 to cavin2 observed in subcomplexes released from caveolae (Figure 4D) is similar to that reported in Ludwig et al. (2013) but notably in the absence of caveolae more variable ratios are observed (Figure 2 in MCF-7 and cell-free systems).
evidence: This is stated based on single-molecule coincidence data after hypo-osmotic treatment (Figure 4D) and compared to another study.

claim: The number of cavin proteins in the caveolar coat is relatively low compared to other protein coats such as clathrin
source: The studies indicate that the number of cavin proteins in the caveolar coat is relatively low, considering the number of CAV1 proteins within a caveola, and compared to the other protein coats such as clathrin (made of 30 + triskelias, approximately 200 subunits).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between caveolar coat (~50 cavins) and clathrin coat (~200 subunits).

claim: Cavin1 forms trimers, possibly through a coiled-coil domain
source: Cavin1 is believed to form trimers, possibly through a coiled-coil domain (Ludwig et al., 2013), suggesting that each sub-complex may be composed of three trimers.
evidence: This is stated with citation to another study.

claim: Cavin1-cavin2 and cavin1-cavin3 subcomplexes are mutually exclusive
source: Our data clearly shows however, that cavin2 and cavin3 are not present in the same assemblies with cavin1: the sub-complexes are mutually exclusive for cavin2 or cavin3.
evidence: Single-molecule analysis after hypo-osmotic treatment shows complete segregation of cavin2 and cavin3 into separate cavin1-containing subcomplexes (Figure 4D-F).

claim: Stable units of cavin1-cavin2 and cavin1-cavin3 can come together on the membrane to regulate the formation of the curved caveolar structure
source: Thus stable units of cavin1-cavin2 and cavin1-cavin3 can come together on the membrane to regulate the formation of the curved caveolar structure.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both subcomplexes localize to the same caveolae but in spatially distinct domains (Figure 5C, 5D).

claim: Large cavin complexes formed in the absence of caveolins may be rare in vivo
source: Expression in cells lacking caveolins may reflect an artificial situation as cavins and caveolins are generally expressed together in vivo. We believe the large complexes formed under these conditions may be rare in vivo, possibly explaining the slow association of expressed cavin with newly-arrived caveolin at the plasma membrane (25 min) when fluorescently-tagged cavin is expressed in mammalian cells (Hayer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that cavin-caveolin association takes 25 minutes in cells, cited from previous work.

claim: Cavin subcomplexes could be pre-assembled rapidly in the cytosol before reaching the CAV1-rich domains at the membrane
source: The fact that oligomers of cavin1 form so readily in the cell-free expression system (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) suggests that the subcomplexes could be pre-assembled rapidly in the cytosol, before reaching the CAV1-rich domains at the membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cavin1 oligomerizes within 15 minutes at nanomolar concentrations in cell-free system (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).

claim: Combined interaction with membranes and caveolin results in recruitment of cavin subcomplexes to budding caveolae
source: We hypothesize that a combined interaction with membranes (Hansen et al., 2009) and caveolin itself will result in recruitment of the subcomplexes to the budding caveolae, where they can be assembled into the striated structures observed on intact caveolae (this study and Ludwig et al., 2013).
evidence: This is hypothesized based on the current findings and cited previous work.

claim: The cavin1/cavin2 and cavin1/cavin3 complexes make up the caveolar striations seen by high resolution SEM and deep etch electron microscopy
source: The preferential labeling of spatially-distinct linear elements raises the possibility that the cavin1/cavin2 and cavin1/cavin3 complexes actually make up the caveolar striations seen by high resolution SEM and deep etch electron microscopy (Peters et al., 1985; Rothberg et al., 1992) consistent with EM observations with miniSOG-cavin fusion proteins (Ludwig et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial segregation observed by immuno-EM (Figure 5C) and comparison with previous structural studies.

claim: Striated nanodomains could be released from caveolae in response to membrane stretch
source: These striated 'nanodomains' could be released from ('peel off') the caveolae/membrane in response to membrane stretch.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that hypo-osmotic treatment releases intact subcomplexes (Figure 4).

claim: Released cavin subcomplexes could potentially reach distinct cellular destinations or interact with different partners
source: We speculate that this could potentially release two distinct subcomplexes, each able to reach distinct cellular destinations or interact with different partners.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that two distinct subcomplexes are released upon membrane stretch.

claim: The properties of individual caveolae can be modulated by their ratio of cavin1, 2, and 3 subcomplexes
source: An additional possibility is that the properties of individual caveolae can be modulated by their ratio of cavin1, 2, and 3 subcomplexes to vary their individual properties, including stability or morphology.
evidence: This is speculated based on the finding that different subcomplexes exist.

claim: The mode of assembly of cytoplasmic caveolar coat proteins is distinct from that of any other known coat complex
source: The mode of assembly of cytoplasmic caveolar coat proteins shown here is distinct from that of any other known coat complex.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the findings and comparison with other coat proteins like clathrin.

claim: Caveolar assembly relies on association of pre-oligomerized cavin subcomplexes that give rise to the unique caveolar striations
source: In contrast to other coat proteins, such as clathrin, which form a very dense basket-like network in a cooperative and stepwise process through protein–protein interactions and binding to membrane components and then is disassembled into individual triskelia in an ATP-dependent process, we hypothesize that caveolar assembly relies on association of pre-oligomerized cavin subcomplexes that give rise to the unique caveolar striations.
evidence: This is hypothesized based on the observation that cavins form stable subcomplexes that can associate with and dissociate from caveolae.

claim: Cavin proteins are cytoplasmic proteins
source: Cavin1/polymerase transcript release factor (PTRF), cavin2/SDPR (serum deprivation response protein), cavin3/SRBC (serum deprivation response factor-related gene product that binds to C-kinase) and cavin4/MURC (muscle-restricted coiled-coil protein) are cytoplasmic proteins characterized by conserved putative N-terminal coiled coil domains (Hansen and Nichols, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of cavin proteins.

claim: Cavins have been linked to many disease conditions including cardiomyopathies, lipodystrophy, and skeletal muscle disorders
source: Like caveolins, cavins have also now been linked to many disease conditions including cardiomyopathies, lipodystrophy, and skeletal muscle disorders (Parton and Del Pozo, 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to a review.

claim: The leakage from GFP to Cherry channel was experimentally determined at 10%
source: For single-molecule coincidence, the coincidence ratio is calculated as Mukhopadhyay et al. (2007) [Intensity(Cherry)−leakage from GFP channel]/total intensity (Intensity (Cherry)+Intensity(GFP)); the leakage from GFP to Cherry channel was experimentally determined at 10%.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: The residence time of GFP monomers in the confocal volume is 100 μs
source: As in the earlier case, the measurement is calibrated by GFP, monomeric at the concentration used (100 pM), which displays a well-defined residence time in the focal volume of 100 μs.
evidence: This is stated as a calibration measurement (also shown in Figure 1F, 1G).

claim: The residence times measured for cavin1 oligomers are approximately 10 times slower than GFP
source: The residence times measured for cavin1 oligomers are approximately 10 times slower than GFP.
evidence: This is stated based on single-molecule FCS measurements (Figure 1I).

claim: The intensity of CAV1-GFP puncta in the cytoplasm is 150 to 200-fold higher than the brightness of a single GFP
source: As shown in Figure 3C, the intensity of these puncta reaches values that are 150 to 200-fold higher than the brightness of a single GFP.
evidence: This is stated based on brightness analysis (Figure 3C).

claim: Caveolae contain up to 180 CAV1 proteins
source: As caveolae contain up to 180 CAV1 proteins, this corresponds well to the expected brightness of fully-assembled caveola (Pelkmans and Zerial, 2005).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: Cavin1 does not associate with CAV1 in non-caveolar cellular compartments
source: As cavin1 does not associate with CAV1 in non-caveolar cellular compartments, such as when CAV1 is moving along the secretory pathway or if caveolae are disassembled (Hill et al., 2008; Hayer et al., 2010) we are confident that these represent bona fide caveolae.
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: The CAV1 signal is 3.5 times brighter than that of cavin1
source: This observation corroborates the brightness analysis that demonstrates that the CAV1 signal is 3.5 times brighter than that of cavin1 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated based on brightness analysis (Figure 3C).

claim: Approximately 15% of cavin1-only oligomers are observed after hypo-osmotic treatment in cavin1-cavin2 co-expression
source: Data show that all cavin2 are bound to cavin1 but approximately 15% of the oligomers contain cavin1 only.
evidence: This is stated based on single-molecule coincidence analysis after hypo-osmotic treatment (Figure 4D).

claim: Approximately 20% of cavin1-only oligomers are observed after hypo-osmotic treatment in cavin1-cavin3 co-expression
source: Data show that all cavin3 are bound to cavin1 and approx. 20% of cavin1-only oligomers are observed.
evidence: This is stated based on single-molecule coincidence analysis after hypo-osmotic treatment (Figure 4E).

claim: Cavin subcomplexes do not form direct interactions in solution
source: The complete lack of co-diffusion indicates that subcomplexes do not form direct interactions in solution; it also suggests that on the membrane, they do not bind strongly to form stable mixed structures.
evidence: This is inferred from the complete segregation of cavin2 and cavin3 after hypo-osmotic treatment (Figure 4F).

claim: Cavin subcomplexes do not bind strongly on the membrane to form stable mixed structures
source: The complete lack of co-diffusion indicates that subcomplexes do not form direct interactions in solution; it also suggests that on the membrane, they do not bind strongly to form stable mixed structures.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that subcomplexes separate completely upon release from membrane.
